phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode` IS an `rclcpp::Node`, so this is `rclcpp::Node::get_publisher_names_and_types_by_node`, inherited, with `cpp:Node::get_publisher_names_and_types_by_node`'s contract. The extractor records only the members a class declares, so this key correlates as upstream-only even though the name resolves.

Before phase-482 W4: phase-417 stage 2b. Same verb as ROS 2; the RECEIVER and the CARRIER differ. ROS 2 hangs the graph off a node because each Node/Context owns a participant; a nano-ros image opens ONE session for the whole image and the Executor owns it (RFC-0002), so `nros::Executor` holds the query and `nros::LifecycleNode` forwards to it (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/node.hpp`) -- that forwarder is what a ported rclcpp file reaches, on the object rclcpp puts it on. Prints ours-only because rclcpp's public NODE surface has no `*_by_node` form for publishers: upstream keeps it on `NodeGraphInterface`, which `public_surface.py` drops as plumbing. And the carrier is a VISITOR (`nros_cpp_names_and_types_visit_fn`, `void *ctx`) where rclcpp returns `std::map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>>` -- no allocator (RFC-0022), so the answer streams one entry at a time instead of being built. See `cpp:Executor::get_publisher_names_and_types_by_node` for the receiver decision and `c:get_publisher_names_and_types_by_node` for the C half. A lifecycle node reaches the graph exactly as an ordinary one does here; see `cpp:Node::get_publisher_names_and_types_by_node`.
